findings.meaning: Ordinary Python fence has no filename/version title. Code body contains executable code and real comments. Source checksum/checkpoint UI is not part of this block.

evidence.text: # Custom state can be passed in invoke

findings.meaning: Only custom state class, state_schema argument and custom input fields are marked with # [!code highlight]. Hosted HTML emits span.line.line-highlight and removes the directive from displayed text.

evidence.text: With [short-term memory](#usage) enabled, long conversations can exceed the LLM's context window. Common solutions are:
Remove first or last N messages (before calling LLM)
Delete messages from LangGraph state permanently
Summarize earlier messages in the history and replace them with a summary

findings.meaning: Two-column cards summarize four related choices. Three have local anchor links and arrow; the fourth is informational. Detailed explanations follow below.

evidence.text: /* Tip-styled cards — match Tip callout (lime #d4e8a8 / olive #8da042) */
/* Make card and dropdown borders visible in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11: 3:1 min for UI components) */

findings.meaning: Normal cards are transparent; optional semantic tip cards get lime color. Dark cards use a visible #4f5d73 border. Color is assigned to component purpose, not every paragraph.
Hosted code uses a cool pale neutral surface, narrow local scrolling, syntax color and targeted lines. No W01/checkpoint/hash text is in the code body.

project_adaptations: Move filename/version/source details and source links outside the pure code surface. Keep a small copy control; keep platform/version tabs only when there is an actual choice, above the surface.
Use the official #eff1f5 code surface as reference. A softer blue-gray whole-page reading background is a user-requested local adaptation, not an official accessibility or eye-fatigue claim.
Add a small F01 request Accept versus response Content-Type comparison, linked to their existing subsections. Keep narrative explanation and source code contiguous.
Use cards for published chapter navigation or F03 definition/import/call concept navigation. Avoid enclosing all prose in cards and avoid fake arrows on nonlinks.

Highlight the one mechanism currently explained: F01 request/status/header lines; F03 def/return versus explicit call and import. Do not highlight all lines or encode teaching completeness through color.

contrast_audit.method: WCAG relative luminance contrast from official hex colors; not browser-computed contrast
contrast_audit.recommendation: Body and code text should be checked at 4.5:1. Darken low-contrast light-theme tokens within the same hue if needed, especially against blue highlighted rows; preserve source text and dark-theme palette.

limitations: No pixel-exact card dimensions or highlighted-row RGB measured from this HTTP review. User screenshots supply the visual reference.
Hosted snippet models and imports can change independently of pinned repository source.
The original Python source checkpoint remains unchanged; display metadata may change without altering example code.
